scope: local / one host / six simulated worker directories / direct Backend calls
notes: DFSIO-inspired, not Hadoop TestDFSIO. Aggregate MiB/s = logical bytes / phase wall time; task_time_mib_s = bytes / sum of operation durations; mean_task_mib_s = mean per-file rate.
Write timing includes seeded pseudorandom generation, CRC32C, bounded streaming, concurrent durable replica writes and namespace commit. Read timing includes full byte-count and CRC32C verification.

Reads follow writes; OS caches are not flushed. The read phase starts with an empty Mammoth cache; read_cached reuses it. Cache counters reveal hits and evictions; neither phase claims cold-disk bandwidth.
Metadata creates empty files, stats, renames and deletes them; it measures the indexed SQLite WAL namespace, not NameNode RPC latency. Empty files do not exercise replication.

Warmups excluded; all measured iterations retained. Latencies exclude waiting for a client slot but include backend contention (eight upload slots per backend; one SQLite writer). Fresh isolated store per iteration; setup and cleanup excluded.

Compute uses fixed 25-byte UTF-8 records (requested size rounded down), parallel line sort and word count with verified outputs. Setup and validation are outside timing; job memory targets, spill bytes and run counts are recorded. This is local compute, not distributed TeraSort.
No Hadoop/Spark baseline, physical network, distributed shuffle or TeraSort result. Rust alone implies no performance advantage.
